name: Burushaski
notes: REGISTRY STUB (not a modelled G2P target). Placed so the ancestry graph covers every living ISO 639-3 language. No orthography is claimed; the phoneme inventory follows the cited PHOIBLE inventory (which itself cites a published description): script is Zyyy (undetermined) until a cited description is encoded. Classification and coordinates follow Glottolog. Checked against lexibank/northeuralex forms.csv for a gold-registration candidate: its `bsk` Value column (e.g. "-lcin", "-ltumal", "-mupus", "qhat", leading hyphens marking bound/possessed noun stems) is written with retroflex-dot diacritics (s-dot, t-dot) and a leading hyphen convention that is Berger's (1998, Die Burushaski-Sprache von Hunza und Nager) scholarly transcription, not a community orthography: Burushaski has no standardized practical spelling (it is variably written in Urdu-based Perso-Arabic script by some literacy efforts, and in ad hoc Latin transliterations by others, neither of which NorthEuraLex's Value column reflects). Per this repo's orthography-vs-transcription distinction, a linguist's IPA-adjacent transcription convention is not "the orthography" a spec's `graphemes` table is supposed to describe, so no graphemes are added and no NorthEuraLex gold row is registered for bsk: registering it would misrepresent Berger's transcription as a citable Burushaski spelling convention. The spec remains a stub with the cited PHOIBLE phoneme inventory only.
